clue.text: V's pivotal point?

parts.note: the letter V sits exactly in the middle of the word gravity, so V is that word's central point, as well as the phrase meaning a balance point in physics

explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase literally: the centre of the seven-letter word GRAVITY is its fourth letter, V. The question mark flags the pun on the physics term.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics this is the point about which a body's weight balances, its pivotal point; literally the middle letter of the word gravity is V.

clue.text: Kings in medical setback almost sent up firework

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up says the whole assembly is read bottom to top
in says the kings sit inside the shortened setback
almost says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a relapse is a setback in a patient's recovery
K and R are both abbreviations for king (R from Latin rex), so two kings give KR

explanation.surface: Monarchs suffering a health relapse somehow launch a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for king from the Latin rex, so 'Kings' supplies two letters. 'sent up' turns the whole assembly upside down, as befits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkler is a hand-held firework that throws off sparks.

clue.text: Capital piece of furniture I acquired

indicators.note: the furniture takes in, or acquires, the letter I

parts.note: a sofa is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A capital-quality item of furniture that the speaker has bought.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Missing person dispatched in the middle of a competition

indicators.note: says the dispatched word goes into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a bee is a competition, as in a spelling bee
something dispatched has been sent

explanation.surface: Someone who has gone missing was sent off partway through a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle of' places the dispatched word partway through the competition piece. A spelling bee is a spelling competition, a sense of 'bee' common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is someone who is not present, a missing person.

clue.text: Setter is, unfortunately, upset by sausage

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the run of pieces is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, so the setter is gives I'M
alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is sorry to be troubled by a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IMALAS round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a type of cured, highly seasoned sausage.

clue.text: Gurn stupidly, probing vagrant's waterworks problem

indicators.note: probing says the jumbled letters push inside the vagrant word

parts.note: a stray is a vagrant; the 's is a link meaning is

indicators.note: stupidly says these letters are jumbled

parts.note: to gurn is to pull a grotesque face

explanation.surface: Someone pulling silly faces while examining a tramp's urinary trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: To gurn is a British word for pulling a grotesque face. 'stupidly' jumbles it and 'probing' sends it into the vagrant word.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangury is a painful, slow discharge of urine, a urinary or waterworks disorder.

clue.text: Reported allegorist's foot ailment

indicators.note: reported signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: John Bunyan wrote the allegory The Pilgrim's Progress

explanation.surface: A rumoured problem with the feet of the author of an allegory.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunion is a painful swelling on the joint of the big toe, an ailment of the foot.

clue.text: Year spoilt by "Les liaisons dangereuses", say?

parts.note: the clue words year spoilt are what you get from the ten letters of the answer's first word when its second word is read as an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A year ruined by reading a scandalous French novel of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: NOVEL signals an anagram of EPISTOLARY, which gives YEAR SPOILT. Laclos's Les Liaisons dangereuses is told entirely in letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Liaisons dangereuses is a famous example of a novel told through letters between characters.

clue.text: Plant finds bachelor in high spirits

indicators.note: in says the bachelor letter goes inside the high spirits word

parts.note: euphoria is a state of elation, high spirits

explanation.surface: A plant puts a single man in a cheerful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is a genus of plants, the spurges, including the poinsettia.

clue.text: Blast old cap!

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a trumpet call
to cap something is to outdo it, beat it with something better

explanation.definitionFit: The archaic sense is a trumpet blast; as a verb it means to beat or outdo, which is what capping a remark does.

clue.text: Born in Italian city, getting energy from motor

indicators.note: in says the born letter goes inside the city

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone born in Turin powered by energy from an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine is a rotary engine driven by a flow of fluid, a kind of motor.

clue.text: Fruit — one swallowed by Biblical liar

indicators.note: says one is taken inside the fruit word

parts.note: ananas is another name for the pineapple
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit eaten by a lying figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: ANANAS, the pineapple, is a word most solvers know only from crosswords or French.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananias in Acts lied about the price of his land and fell dead; his name came to mean a liar.

clue.text: Fitzgerald's desanctified lager?

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for saint is removed, so the word is no longer holy

parts.note: Stella Artois is a well-known brand of lager

explanation.surface: F. Scott Fitzgerald's beer, stripped of any holiness.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the standard abbreviation for saint; removing it from STELLA leaves the first name of the jazz singer Ella Fitzgerald.
explanation.definitionFit: The jazz singer Ella Fitzgerald is the best-known person with this surname.

clue.text: Speeding up sequence before finish and start of oratorio

parts.note: a string is a sequence or series
an end is a finish

indicators.note: start of says only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A musical sequence accelerating before the close and the opening of a choral work.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringendo is a musical direction meaning gradually speeding up the tempo.

clue.text: Drips spilled on cooker shown to be a mistake

indicators.note: spilled says the letters of drips are scattered into a new order

parts.note: an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: Water dripping onto the stove proves something wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disproven has been shown to be false, an error.

clue.text: Likely to carry part of five-litre flask back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer lies inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that may hold a share of a large flask returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'part' in the definition, but 'part of' signals the letters ELITREF inside 'five-litre flask'; 'back' reads them in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Fertile means able to bear offspring or crops, likely to carry young.

clue.text: A bitter blow for head of the Church?

indicators.note: blow is used in the sense of blow apart, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A bitter setback suffered by the leader of the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' turns A BITTER into the answer. The definition is cryptic: a biretta is a square cap worn on a clergyman's head, a head covering of the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is a stiff square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy, so it belongs on a churchman's head.

clue.text: Unpolished jewellery put outside for scrapping

indicators.note: says the jewellery word is placed round the unpolished one

parts.note: bling is flashy jewellery
something unpolished is raw or crude

explanation.surface: Rough jewels placed outside to be thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put outside' wraps the jewellery word round the unpolished one. Bling is slang for showy jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawling is fighting noisily, the same as scrapping in its sense of fighting.

clue.text: Arab money raised by part of factory

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised says the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: a Moor is a North African of Arab or Berber descent
loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: Arab cash lifted by a section of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns MOORLOOT round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolroom is the workshop area in a factory where tools are made and kept.

clue.text: Two-way processing of force's third police car

indicators.note: third picks the third letter of the word force
processing says the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The third member of a police force processing a squad car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third' takes R from 'force'; 'processing of' shuffles R and POLICE CAR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Reciprocal means mutual, given and received in both directions.

clue.text: True Church in wrong order for breakfast, perhaps

indicators.note: says the two pieces are written in the opposite order to the clue

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England
real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: A genuine church service held at the wrong time, around breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal is a typical breakfast food, so breakfast with 'perhaps' points to an example.

clue.text: Fixate on love — Porgy's — capturing heart of music

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: says the Porgy word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Bess is Porgy's partner in Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess

indicators.note: heart of picks the middle letter of the word music

explanation.surface: Becoming fixated on the love story of Porgy, gripped by the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts S, the middle letter of 'music', inside BESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess is to fixate on something, dwelling on it compulsively.

clue.text: Fish round in air

indicators.note: in says the round letter goes inside the air word

parts.note: to air washing is to dry it
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A fish going round in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A dory is a sea fish, such as the John Dory.

clue.text: Accent displaying perspicacity

definitions.meaning: the accent mark sloping up to the right over a vowel, as in é
showing sharp insight or keen perception

explanation.definitionFit: It names both a diacritic mark and the quality of being sharp-witted or perceptive.

clue.text: Saviour resurrected by divers, formerly

indicators.note: the Saviour risen again comes back in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Christ brought back to life by deep-sea divers in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not people who dive but an old word for several or assorted, as in 'divers ways'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective divers means several or of different kinds.

clue.text: Crazy about a service in Swiss town

indicators.note: about says the crazy word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Madness over a church service in a Swiss resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Locarno is a town in southern Switzerland on Lake Maggiore.

clue.text: Exchange of clientele

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both commerce or swapping, and the customers a business serves.

clue.text: Knots sure to come undone as result of overexposure

indicators.note: knots that come undone loosen, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Knots certain to work loose after too long outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunstroke is illness caused by too much exposure to the sun.
